Good morning, Luciana. I am Anna Keller. I manage partnerships in Latin America for a European technology group. Thank you for your time.
Good morning, Anna. Thank you for the invitation. I am the CEO of Teleinfo, a family-owned company in Brazil.
Nice to meet you. So, what does Teleinfo do, exactly?
We specialize in infrastructure: structured cabling, cameras, access control and data centers. Most of our clients are hospitals.
Hospitals are exactly our focus. We are looking for a local partner in Brazil this year. Which hospitals do you work with?
Our client base includes Einstein, Sírio-Libanês, HCor and Oswaldo Cruz. We manage the projects end to end.
That is a strong track record. Our group has offices in Munich and Madrid, and at the moment we are opening an office in São Paulo.
Great timing. We want to expand with international partners. I will send you our company profile after the call.

I manage partners for an American technology company, and every month I talk to about ten new local partners. Many of them start with a long history of the company: the year it started, the first office, the first client. I understand, but I do not have time for that in the first minute. I want three simple things. First, what does your company do? Cabling, cameras, data centers? Second, who are your main clients? Hospitals, banks, factories? And third, what are you working on at the moment? That last question tells me if you are growing. When a partner answers those three questions in one minute, I usually want a second meeting.

I am the IT director of a hospital in London. About four thousand people work here, day and night. People think a hospital is doctors and nurses, and of course it is. But behind the doctors there is a network. Every machine, every camera and every door depends on it. If the network stops, the hospital stops. That is why we work with specialists. A good infrastructure partner knows that a hospital never closes. This year my team is building a new data center, and we are changing the access control in the old building. We are doing all of it without closing a single room.

Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome back. Before the break, a quick introduction of our next three speakers. Our first company is from India. It builds software for hospitals, and it works with more than two hundred clinics. Our second company is from Australia. It specializes in security cameras, and this year it is opening its first office in Europe. And our third company is from Brazil. It provides infrastructure for hospitals and data centers. I asked each speaker for the same thing: present your company in one minute, and tell us what you are working on now. So please, keep your eyes on the clock. Let us begin.
